verificationNote: No build or test was run. 'Verified' means I read it from source or measured it with the clock probe below. 'Inference' means I reasoned it and did not execute it.

clockProbe.method: A python3 parent wrote one line at a time to `docker run --rm -i node:22-bookworm sh -c 'while read x; do date -u +%s.%N; done'`. Each read was bracketed by host time.time(). offset = vm - midpoint, and the bound is half the round trip. n=40. The first attempt used alpine, but busybox date has no %N, so it was discarded.
clockProbe.result: At 2026-10-13T17:18:39Z, VM minus host = median -0.30 ms, range -0.44 to +1.45 ms. The minimum-RTT sample was -0.37 ms ± 0.64 ms. Host load average at the time was 14.9/9.5/8.3.
interpretation: Verified: with no recent sleep, the Docker VM clock (the clock Testcontainers Postgres reads) is within about 1 ms of the host, and is usually slightly behind it.

Inference: that sub-millisecond lag is enough to trip a zero-tolerance issuedAt <= clock_timestamp() check. The fixture mints issuedAt with the host clock, truncates it to the millisecond, and INSERTs it within the same millisecond or so. This explains ProgressCallbackIT's 2 setup failures with no host sleep. The 13-minute post-sleep lag in the authz-grant ledger is the same mechanism at a larger magnitude.

rulings.question: Is zero skew tolerance between the JVM-minted issuedAt and the DB now() correct?
rulings.decision: Zero tolerance is the correct rule. The defect is that two clocks feed it. Option B is chosen: replay-grant times are minted and judged on the database clock. The trigger stays byte-identical, with no tolerance, no TTL change and no migration. The JVM clock no longer participates in any grant decision.

verified: Trigger V15 L388 on INSERT raises 'observed execution grant expired' when expiresAt <= clock_timestamp() OR issuedAt > clock_timestamp(). L386 requires issuedAt <= expiresAt <= issuedAt + 30 s.

The same two-clock comparison appears at V15 L341-342 (retry rebinding: issuedAt <= clock_timestamp() AND expiresAt > clock_timestamp()) and at L409-410 (first receipt: admittedAt >= issuedAt AND expiresAt > clock_timestamp()).

ObservedReplayAuthorizer L68 mints issuedAt from the JVM clock, and L77 checks the ceiling against the JVM clock. ObservedReplayAuthorization L179 (refreshRetry) mints from the JVM clock. L229 (check, called from bind/prepareAdmission/job/claimObserved) and L116 (the prepareAdmission 5 s cap) judge against the JVM clock. Production wiring hard-codes Clock.systemUTC() in both configuration classes, not the Spring Clock bean.

Every other grant-time decision already uses the DB clock: AdmissionCasService.claimObserved reads SELECT clock_timestamp() for admittedAt and the permit expiry, and StudioDispatchLedgerStatements beginDispatch checks expiresAt > clock_timestamp(). Two guided stores already use a SELECT clock_timestamp() wall clock.
Production runs 3-6 API replicas (SnapshotBroadcaster/WatchedExecutionRegistry javadoc) plus workers. They each have their own JVM clock and share one Postgres.

The authz-grant ledger reproduced the run1 signature with the JVM 2 s and 788 s ahead of the DB. The r8-selfstop ledger shows ProgressCallbackIT failing at the fixture INSERT (GuidedSecretLoginMigrationTest.publishedRetry mints issuedAt = Instant.now()) with no host sleep.
inferred: The issuedAt-not-in-the-future clause is exactly what bounds the DB-measured residual life of a grant to 30 s. At INSERT, expiresAt - dbNow = 30 s + skew - (insert - mint latency). Refusing issuedAt > dbNow forces skew <= latency, so the residual is <= 30 s. Any tolerance tau lets a grant minted on a clock that is ahead live up to 30 s + tau by the DB clock, which lengthens the window.

optionsConsidered.summary: Bounded future-skew tolerance tau on issuedAt only (issuedAt > clock_timestamp() + tau).
why: It lengthens the DB-measured window by up to tau when the minting clock is ahead (see the inference above). That violates the 'never lengthened' constraint.
It does not cover the observed post-sleep skew (788 s) unless tau is absurd.
The Java checks would still use a different clock from the trigger, so a JVM behind the DB still turns a correct refusal into a raw JpaSystemException (500) instead of 409 AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED.

optionsConsidered.summary: A tolerance of tau plus a TTL shortened by tau.
optionsConsidered.why: It changes the TTL semantics, still fails for skew > tau, and still keeps two clocks.

optionsConsidered.summary: Mint issuedAt and judge expiry on the DB clock (SELECT clock_timestamp()), so a single clock decides.
why: One authority, the same one the trigger, dispatch CAS and admission CAS already use. It is independent of the number of replicas.

The security property is preserved exactly and becomes tighter: the DB-measured life is <= 30 s from issuance, and the zero-tolerance clause stays as a guard against forged or buggy future-dated grants.
No SQL change. The trigger is not touched, so there is no V15 edit and no V19+ ordering question.

Small change surface: a Clock implementation and two wiring lines. The authorizer and authorization keep their Clock constructor parameter, so the Clock.fixed component tests (ObservedAdmissionSecurityIT, ObservedResolverProcessCrashIT, ObservedReadEntryProtocolIT, StudioDispatcherFailureIT) keep their meaning: the fixed clock models the DB clock.

optionsConsidered.summary: Let the DB stamp issuedAt inside the INSERT (default or trigger-assigned).
optionsConsidered.why: The grant is minted in authorize() outside any transaction, after BFF account freshness and before the acceptance transaction. It is then schema-validated and bound by hash into the binding. Stamping at INSERT would split the grant's identity across two moments and move authority into DDL.

rulings.question: Is the post-Ready control-window miss in C6 kind 1 correct fail-closed behaviour, a product timing defect, or a test-instrumentation defect?
rulings.decision: The runner's self-stop is correct fail-closed behaviour and stays unchanged. The miss is not tolerated by the test. The failure is environmental (load about 7). A verified test-instrumentation defect amplifies it: the producer-2 preload runs synchronous file I/O, including fsyncSync, inside the runner parent's control-read critical path, ahead of the runner's own window check. Fix the instrumentation and make a window miss an explicit, attributable precondition failure. No product timing defect was proven. One latent product synchronous-ps path was found and is deferred (R10-OBS-1).

verified: Each secret-bearing window is [nextPoll, nextPoll + 1000 - 25) on absolute time. A late timer, a slow /control response, or a non-200 or invalid body each self-stop with source 'control-window' (runCoordinator L386-405). The control poll runs until the execute() finally (L744-748), so it is live during runSession.execute(), session.close() and the kill await.

After Ready, a self-stop calls control.end = endRun('cancel') -> runSession.kill('cancel'). The child then reports a cancelled failure kind, which produces outer CANCELLED. In run 2 the self-stop therefore happened before the child's own result (the step-deadline OUTCOME_UNKNOWN) reached the parent.

For kind 1, state.path = 2 (p8C6Run constructs P4RevocationState(..., kind <= 2 ? 2 : 1, ...)). The producer-2 wrapper (p4OrdinaryRevocationHttp, loaded into the runner parent) therefore selects every control GET.

Wrapper behaviour, in this order: (i) at every send it calls revMode() synchronously, which is existsSync plus readFileSync plus JSON.parse. (ii) It attaches result.then(...) to the runner's request promise before returning it, so its reaction runs before the runner's own `await Promise.race(...)` continuation. (iii) That reaction runs revEmit (revInit, with lstatSync/realpathSync on the first call of a case) and, in its finally, revPublish: lstatSync, realpathSync, existsSync, openSync, writeFileSync, fsyncSync, closeSync, renameSync. All of this is synchronous on the parent event loop, and all of it happens between the /control response and the runner's `options.now() >= windowEnd` check.
revEmit's own finally runs revPublish (synchronous, with fsync) again when the observer ACK settles, which blocks the loop again between ticks.

Product parent work during the run: trackTree samples with an asynchronous ps every 25 ms, with no overlap (launcher L250-255). The child-output redactor is createRedactor([]). c5ProfileScan (a synchronous profile walk) runs only at context close (child) and scratch clear (parent), both after the outcome, not mid-run.
The test's observer HttpServer uses a virtual-thread-per-task executor (L611). Handlers take synchronized(state).
inferred: Run 2 is a race between the window check and the combined latency: the JVM-hosted /control round trip at load about 7, plus fsync and stat latency under heavy I/O (Docker VM, Chromium video, Gradle). The available log line cannot split these. It names neither the branch nor the latency.

Timing coincidence, not measured: browser start 16:10:37Z and self-stop 16:11:13Z (+36 s) are close to fill start + 30 s step timeout. A miss at the step-deadline cut, when child IPC, progress POSTs and instrumentation events burst together, is plausible.

change.owner: @dev (Dex, R8/runner lane, which already holds GuidedPublicationReplayIT). No product file changes.
required: I1. Producer-2 must not run instrumentation work synchronously in the runner parent's control-read path. (a) Replace the per-send synchronous revMode() read in p4OrdinaryRevocationHttp with a cached mode, refreshed asynchronously. The existing watchFile(25 ms) pattern is acceptable. The Java side writes the mode before dispatch, and the first secret control read is at least 1 s after admission. (b) Do not register a reaction on the runner's own request promise that does synchronous I/O. Observe the outcome from a separate branch whose work is deferred with setImmediate. (c) Move revPublish for producer 2 to fs/promises (open with O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, write, filehandle.sync(), close, rename), serialized on a promise chain. File modes, confinement checks, event sequence, counts and 'sent == acked' semantics stay identical.

I2. Value-free timing evidence for attribution. In the same wrapper, record per selected control read the performance.now() deltas (send to settle). Run a perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay histogram for the life of the selected case. Publish the max and p99 loop delay, plus the count and max of control-read durations, as numeric fields in the producer sample. This needs a schema bump of the sample's fixed key count in the Java check at L8768. That check counts fields and is not an assertion about the product.

I3. Explicit precondition in p8C6Run, kind 1 (and kind 2, which asserts a recorded public cancel on the same secret-bearing path). After p3AwaitExecution and before the outcome assertions, assert that the runner log for this execution has zero run.cancel_requested with source 'control-window'. Message: 'PRECONDITION: secret control window held; a miss is the runner fail-closed self-stop (host load), not this scenario'. Include the I2 numbers in the description. This adds an assertion and the test still FAILs. Nothing is tolerated.

rulings.question: The lost-ack instrumentation issue (run 3: producer 3 sent 4, acked 3, failed:true; child ended before Ready).
rulings.decision: Not an independent defect. It is a symptom. The primary event in run 3 was a pre-Ready end of the observed child. The producer-3 wrapper is designed to mark failed on a pre-Ready stop, and the in-flight observer POST died with the child. Do not change the ack path or the 1000 ms observer timeout. Make the c6Pending wait failure attributable, and recover run 3's reason.

verified: Producer 3 (p4OrdinaryRevocationChild) is loaded into the observed child. Its 'stop' listener throws 'READY' when !revReady || !revStarted and then calls revFail() -> failed:true. Its exit wrapper calls revFail() for c6 when !revC6Restored and publishes the sealed sample. A pre-Ready stop therefore always produces failed:true with any POST in flight unacknowledged.

Ledger: no run.cancel_requested for that execution, browser_started false, last_runner_sequence 1, ledger DONE, error_code NULL. That is the R8 pre-Ready RUN_ERROR shape, with a launcher reason from the R8-ADJ-2 set.

inferred: The most likely reason is TIMEOUT: the pre-Ready wait expired under load and the child launch (persistent Chromium context) was slow. This is correct fail-closed behaviour. It is not verified, because the FINAL errorMessage was not captured in the ledger.

rulings.question: R8-OBS-1: should a post-Ready unrecorded self-stop report RUN_ERROR (consistent with R8) or stay CANCELLED? In 012A or deferred?
rulings.decision: In principle it should be RUN_ERROR. R8.1's rule ('outer CANCELLED only for a stop the API recorded') applies equally after Ready. The change is DEFERRED out of 012A to STUDIO-OBS-009, beside R8-ADJ-1. 012A keeps today's post-Ready CANCELLED.
why: No API-visible difference today (verified, RunnerOutcomeCodes L80-92): a runner CANCELLED without a recorded cancel or revocation maps to error_code NULL, and RUN_ERROR also maps to NULL. No strand: post-Ready FINALs are accepted. The deferral has no security impact, and the run is stopped either way.

It interacts with revocation mapping. A run with a recorded revocation whose control read is then lost currently reports runner CANCELLED, which the API maps to AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED. Moving to RUN_ERROR would lose that mapping unless the R8 `recorded` upgrade is extended to revocation facts. That needs a security-reviewed design, which is OBS-009 territory (AC-11).

It needs a post-Ready shape decision with no new vocabulary: the outer errorMessage reason, the interrupted step's failure (the child's stop reason 'CANCELLED' or STOPPED_STEP_MESSAGE), and projection pins.
It would not fix R10. Kind 1 would still fail, because the errorMessage and step failure would not be OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
rulings.owner: @po records it in STUDIO-OBS-009 as an AC item, with R10-OBS-2 attached. @architect rules the shape there. @dev implements it there.
stopConditions: Any 012A edit to the post-Ready self-stop classification, to RunnerReportProjection post-Ready acceptance, or to errorCodeFor. Stop.

adjacentFindings.what: StudioAcceptanceService L370-418 takes acceptedAt (started_at, execution_accepted_at, pending_deadline_at = acceptedAt + 600 s SLA) from the JVM clock, but the dispatch CAS judges pending_deadline_at against clock_timestamp(). adjacentFindings.what: The runner's submitObserved (runCoordinator L999) calls validateObservedJob with the runner's own Date.now(), and observedReplay.ts L427 requires issuedAt <= now with zero tolerance. A runner clock behind the minting clock by more than the mint-to-submit latency (acceptance + dispatch + Vault, typically tens of ms or more) gives 409 AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED. R9 does not change this exposure; it only swaps the JVM clock for the DB clock. The post-admission check (L557) uses admittedAt, which is DB-clock and consistent.
adjacentFindings.disposition: Not changed in 012A. The probe shows the test VM lags the host, which is the benign direction. Runbook (STUDIO-OBS-010): runner, API and DB hosts NTP-synced; a stated bound is owed by Platform/SRE.

adjacentFindings.what: launcher.ts kill() (L293-300) calls signalProcessTree(pid,'SIGKILL'). Its default table argument (tree.ts L232) is the synchronous readProcessTable(), which is spawnSync('ps') with a 5000 ms timeout. It is reachable on IPC violation (L450) and on stop-grace exhaustion (L466) while the secret control poll is still live, i.e. before execute() resolves for cancel, total-runtime or drain kills. This is the same starvation class the trackTree fix removed. It is not implicated in R10: the kind-1 outcome was decided before any kill.
adjacentFindings.disposition: Deferred, because changing tree enumeration on the kill path is safety-critical (orphaned Chromium) and quiesce() already re-enumerates asynchronously. @po records a follow-up for OBS-009 or the runner hardening item. The fix direction is to pass the latest asynchronous sample table or await readProcessTableAsync. Do not change the signals.

adjacentFindings.what: The run.cancel_requested log for 'control-window' does not say which of the four branches fired (no request budget, no timer budget, window passed, invalid or non-200 body) and carries no lateness or duration. Production operators cannot attribute a self-stop.
adjacentFindings.disposition: Deferred with R10c to OBS-009. It touches the same log semantics, uses only value-free numeric fields, and is not needed for 012A, because R10a I2 gives test-side attribution.

tradeoffs: R9 option B costs one more DB round trip per clock read (about 5 per Run) and makes grant issuance depend on DB reachability, which a Run needs anyway. In return there is exactly one clock across 3-6 replicas and the trigger stays untouched. Option A would have been a one-line SQL change but lengthens the window and keeps two clocks.

R10 keeps the runner fail-closed at the cost of possible test flakiness under host load. The flakiness is made explicit and attributable (I3 and I2) instead of hidden by tolerance. The instrumentation fix removes the one perturbation the tests themselves introduce.

R10c deferral leaves the wire label CANCELLED for a self-stop after Ready, so wire honesty is not yet complete. The API outcome is unchanged and correct (NULL error_code), and the revocation mapping is preserved until a reviewed design replaces it.
